[[File:Former National Cancer Institute director Arthur Upton (1977 - 1979) (1).jpg|thumb|Arthur C. Upton]]
'''Arthur Canfield Upton''' (February 27, 1923 – February 14, 2015) was an American pathologist and [[Radiobiology|radiation biologist]]. He was former director of the [[National Cancer Institute]] and known for his research in radiation biology of cancer.<ref>{{cite web |title=Arthur C. Upton, MD |url=https://www.aacr.org/professionals/membership/aacr-academy/fellows/arthur-c-upton-md/ |website=American Association for Cancer Research (AACR) |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=AAAS Member Arthur Upton, Expert in Radiation Effects on Human Health, Dead at 91 |url=https://www.aaas.org/news/aaas-member-arthur-upton-expert-radiation-effects-human-health-dead-91 |website=AAAS News}}</ref><ref name=jrp></ref>

== Education and career ==
Upton was born in [[Ann Arbor, Michigan]]. His interest in medicine was ignited after seeing his mother recover from [[pneumonia]]. He studied at [[Phillips Academy in Andover]], Massachusetts. Upton obtained his Bachelor's degree from [[University of Michigan]] and his MD from the [[Michigan Medicine|University of Michigan Medical School]] in 1946. He completed his residency in 1949 in Michigan. From 1951 to 1954, Upton worked as a pathologist at the [[Oak Ridge National Laboratory]] (ORNL).<ref name=carter></ref> He was the Chief of the Pathology-Physiology Section of the Biology Division of the ORNL from 1954 to 1969. Afterwards, Upton was professor of pathology at [[Stony Brook University]] from 1969 to 1977. He was the dean of the School of Basic Health Sciences at Stony Brook University from 1970 to 1975. Between 1965 and 1966, he was the president of the [[Radiation Research Society]].<ref name=jrp>{{cite journal |last1=Boice |first1=John D |title=Arthur C Upton (1923–2015)—In Memoriam |journal=Journal of Radiological Protection |date=2015 |volume=35 |issue=2 |pages=473–475 |doi=10.1088/0952-4746/35/2/473|doi-access=free |pmid=26052879 |bibcode=2015JRP....35..473B }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Boice |first1=John D. |title=In Memoriam: Arthur C. Upton (1923–2015) |journal=Radiation Research |date=April 2015 |volume=183 |issue=4 |pages=485–486 |doi=10.1667/RR00AU.1|pmid=25844947 |bibcode=2015RadR..183..485B |s2cid=27505504 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Arthur C. Upton {{!}} Michigan Medicine |url=https://www.michiganmedicine.org/medicine-michigan/arthur-c-upton |website=www.michiganmedicine.org |language=en |date=15 October 2015}}</ref>

In 1977, President [[Jimmy Carter]] appointed Upton as the director of the [[National Cancer Institute]], who stayed until 1980.<ref name=carter>{{Cite web |title=Appointment of Arthur C. Upton as Director of the National Cancer Institute {{!}} The American Presidency Project |url=https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/appointment-arthur-c-upton-director-the-national-cancer-institute |access-date=2023-10-28 |website=www.presidency.ucsb.edu}}</ref> He moved to [[New York University School of Medicine]] in 1980 and became the Director of the Institute of Environmental Medicine from 1980 to 1992. He then moved to [[University of New Mexico]] and became a clinical professor of pathology and radiology from 1992 to 1995.<ref name=jrp></ref>
